title: Real-Frequency Diagrammatics with Pole Representations
authors: Rayan Farid, Lei Zhang, Aiman Al-Eryani, Agnieszka Jażdżewska, Emanuel Gull
abstract: Finite-temperature many-body theories are typically formulated in imaginary time, where they are amenable to efficient numerical treatment. However, the extraction of spectral properties from the imaginary axis is difficult and requires numerical analytic continuation, while a direct formulation on the real axis requires prohibitively expensive numerical quadrature. In this paper, we represent the objects of many-body perturbation theory using systematically improvable pole and moment expansions and develop the corresponding framework for evaluating diagrammatic contributions directly on the real axis. We introduce a controlled recompression procedure that prevents the proliferation of poles under algebraic and diagrammatic operations. We benchmark the approach on paradigmatic quantum impurity problems and apply it to self-consistent calculations of the uniform electron gas. The resulting spectral quantities converge systematically towards numerical accuracy. This work provides a practical framework for controlled and systematically improvable calculations of spectral quantities within diagrammatic many-body theories, including self-consistent conserving approaches.
summary: This paper develops a novel theoretical framework to calculate spectral properties in many-body physics directly on the real frequency axis, circumventing the numerical instability of analytic continuation. It achieves this by representing Green's functions using systematically improvable pole expansions and defining algebraic rules for complex diagrammatic operations. This provides a robust, controlled tool for advanced calculations in correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is extracting reliable spectral properties from finite-temperature many-body theories, as standard methods relying on analytic continuation from imaginary time are ill-conditioned.
main_result: The authors introduce a practical, controlled, and systematically improvable framework to calculate spectral quantities directly on the real axis, bypassing the need for problematic analytic continuation.
method: The approach represents Green's functions using systematically improvable pole and moment expansions, developing algebraic rules for diagrammatic operations directly on these pole data tuples.
model_or_system: The theory applies to finite-temperature many-body systems, utilizing concepts from diagrammatic perturbation theory (like GW and GF2 self-energies) and the Keldysh formalism.
key_observables: Spectral function ($A_X(\omega)$), retarded/advanced Green's functions ($G_R, G_A$), and self-energies ($\Sigma$).
important_parameters: Finite temperature ($ eta$), frequency ($\omega$), and the number of poles ($M_X$) used in the approximation.
main_assumptions: The method approximates continuous spectral features (branch cuts) by shifting poles into the complex plane, and it relies on a controlled recompression procedure to manage pole proliferation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Keldysh contour, diagrammatic building blocks, and the analytic structure of the spectral function showing poles and branch cuts. A key figure compares the convergence of convolution integrals calculated via pole representation versus numerical quadrature.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of real-axis spectral calculation, introduces the pole/moment expansion framework, details the algebraic rules for diagrammatic operations (convolution, product), and benchmarks the method on impurity models and the uniform electron gas.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter, the rigorous mathematical framework for handling spectral functions via pole expansions is a powerful, general technique for any field requiring accurate spectral analysis, including those involving quantum optics or open systems.

Convergence of the self-consistent iterations for the retarded self-energy of an Anderson impurity model describing a local impurity with U/t = 2 coupled to a semicircular density of states at inverse temperature βt = 10. First iteration shown in light pink, subsequent iterations indicated by progressively darker shades. Number of poles determined by an adaptive recompression scheme to reach accuracy of 10−12. FIG. 7. Validation of the real-frequency results against independent Matsubara calculations, for the same choice of parameters as in Fig. 6. Top row: Im Σ(iωn) for (a) GF2, (b) IPT, and (c) GW at the first iteration (light pink) and for the converged solution (dark purple). Open circles represent the real-axis result back-transformed to imaginary frequency and solid lines are the Matsubara result with parameters ε = 10−14 and Λ = 80. Bottom row (d)–(f): absolute deviation |∆Σ(iωn)|/U 2 between the two calculations.
